title: Framework strict-quotient proper/open exchange
statement: For an open compactification diagram G [def-zl-compactification-open-diagram], a prime $\ell$ different from the characteristic of its finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], and a finite coefficient extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], put $R=\mathcal O_E$. Use the framework completed coefficient sheaf, its finite quotients and simultaneous strict quotient tower [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Define the framework proper mate from the actual derived pull/push adjunction and the framework coefficient-square compositor. Define the open comparison from openDerivedAdjunction, as the inverse of its unit transpose. Form these same mates in the derived category of entire strict diagrams, proper first and then open, and apply total derived inverse limit. The strict source and target identifications are the canonical constant-diagram mates for inverse image, open extension and proper direct image; the proper comparison is their adjunction conjugate, retaining units and counits. Their square with the ambient framework ordered mate commutes, on every strict diagram and hence on the simultaneous quotients of a flat K-flat representative. Define the pullback endpoint realization by the unique quotient-unit chain map whose first Roos coordinate at every quotient is $1\otimes x$ on inverse-image generators and whose shifted coordinate is zero. Its derived map on good complexes determines the open-pullback realization uniquely. Use this realization and the projection-normalized sfQcqsCompactSupportRealization, including sfCompactSupportFiniteReductionIso [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], to define Ex_sf between the recorded framework support and completed-pullback endpoints [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. This construction and its specifications use no PBC coefficient-presentation equivalence or framework/PBC endpoint comparison.
